solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: County in northern half of US state

indicators.note: in a down clue the northern half of a word is its top half, which is its first half

parts.note: Kentucky is a state of the USA

explanation.surface: A geography question about some county in the top half of an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: KENTUCKY has eight letters; its first four are the top half in a down entry. Kent is an English county in the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Kent is a county in south-east England, so it is one example of the general word.

clue.text: Roams foolishly over southern marsh

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, so it comes first
doing something foolishly suggests disorder, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone wanders aimlessly across a bog in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' rearranges ROAMS into MORAS, and 'over' puts that above S in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a boggy, swampy piece of ground, a synonym for a marsh.

clue.text: Leave former partner with the thing

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
it is the pronoun for a thing

explanation.surface: Someone is told to walk away from an old flame and whatever goes with them.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to go out or depart, a synonym of the verb leave.

clue.text: Textbook of the highest quality, latest from professor

parts.note: prime meat or prime goods are of top quality

indicators.note: the latest part of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of professor is used

explanation.surface: Praise for a first-rate textbook, the newest one put out by an academic.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is an elementary textbook, originally one for learning to read.

clue.text: Dismisses those on register

definitions.meaning: to cashier an officer is to dismiss them from the armed forces in disgrace
people who work at a cash register in a shop or bank

explanation.definitionFit: Cashiers is both a verb for sacking someone dishonourably and the plural of the job title of till staff.

clue.text: Fellow Mormon, I suspect, is here in Cornwall

parts.note: bod is informal British slang for a person or fellow

indicators.note: used as an adjective, suspect means doubtful or not genuine, so the letters before it are reworked

explanation.surface: A speaker suspects a fellow Mormon is somewhere in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' makes MINMOOR from the Mormon and the I. Bodmin Moor is a granite upland in Cornwall, the county at England's south-western tip; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodmin Moor is a large moorland area in Cornwall, so it is a place to be found there.

clue.text: Medley of extras on a musical instrument

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so the letters that follow are mixed up

explanation.surface: A jazz soloist plays a mixture of bonus tunes on their instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medley of' shuffles the eight letters of EXTRAS ON; the 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor sax is a mid-range member of the saxophone family, an instrument used in jazz.

clue.text: A network of agents from Yugoslavia initially planted in Spa?

indicators.note: something planted in a thing is put inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a spa is a town with a mineral spring, and a spring is a spa

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the first letter of Yugoslavia is used

explanation.surface: A Yugoslav-run group of agents sets up undercover at a health resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Spa looks like the Belgian town; it is a common noun for a spring. Y goes inside SPRING.
explanation.definitionFit: A spy ring is an organised group of secret agents working together.

clue.text: Cause of timeless crime?

indicators.note: less means without, so time, abbreviated to T, is taken out

parts.note: treason, betraying one's country, is a crime

explanation.surface: A philosophical question about what lies behind an ageless crime.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the usual abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason is the cause or grounds for something happening.

clue.text: Hot and humid in the South (side close to Sicily)

parts.note: a side in sport is a team

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so the last letter of Sicily is taken

explanation.surface: A weather report for Italy's south, near Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as a geographical aside, but it supplies TEAM and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy weather is hot and moist, as full of steam as a humid day.

clue.text: Midget's mouth treated by doctor after end of fight

indicators.note: the rest of the wordplay comes after the letter from fight
the end of a word is its last letter, so only that of fight is used
treated as in processed or worked on, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A small fighter's mouth is patched up by the ringside doctor after the bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' gives OMTHU. The 's stands for 'is'. Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of an English folk tale, a byword for a very small person.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Thumb is a folk-tale character no bigger than his father's thumb, so his name is used for a tiny person.

clue.text: One altering certain features in a theatre?

definitions.text: One altering certain features in a theatre?

parts.words: One altering certain features in a theatre?
parts.note: the features are facial features and the theatre is an operating theatre, not a stage where a make-up artist works

explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic surgeon reshapes faces and bodies, working in a hospital operating theatre.

clue.text: Orlando excited one heroine

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so the word before is rearranged

explanation.surface: An Orlando, perhaps the hero of an old romance, gets excited about a heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges ORLANDO into LORNADO. Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel set on Exmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorna Doone is the title heroine of a classic Victorian romance novel.

clue.text: Petty quarrel about river fish

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a spat is a brief, trivial argument

explanation.surface: Anglers have a minor row about a small fish caught in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river fish' reads as one phrase, but river only gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: The sprat is a small silvery sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Boast about column

parts.note: C, from Latin circa, is an abbreviation for about
a column or file of people or things can be a row

explanation.surface: Someone brags about a newspaper column.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast or gloat loudly, like a cockerel crowing.

clue.text: Inform in advance about travelling fair and a drug

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to warn is to tell someone beforehand of danger

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving about, so the letters of fair are moved around

explanation.surface: Visitors to a travelling funfair are told in advance about a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' gives FARI, and 'about' wraps the warning round it; 'and' is a link, leaving 'a drug' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfarin is an anticoagulant medicine used to prevent blood clots, and also a rat poison.

clue.text: A cinch, right? Wrong!

indicators.note: wrong here means put wrongly, so the letters of the word are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone says something is easy, asks if they are correct, and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A cinch' looks like 'an easy task'; it is the strap that holds a saddle on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinch is a saddle girth, the band fastened round a horse's belly, chiefly in American use.

clue.text: List on counter in repair shop

parts.note: a ship that heels lists or leans over
a bar is a counter where drinks or services are served

explanation.surface: A list of goods kept on the counter at a repair shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A heel bar is a British high-street booth that repairs shoes while you wait.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel bar is a small shop or counter where shoes are mended and keys cut.

clue.text: See opener in Solheim Cup

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, so S from Solheim is taken

parts.note: a cup won as a trophy is a pot in sporting slang

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch the opening match of a women's golf tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solheim Cup is the biennial women's golf contest between Europe and the USA; here the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see or notice it.

clue.text: How chess players sit at every level?

definitions.meaning: two players face each other on opposite sides of the chessboard
an idiom for applying to everyone or everything, at all grades

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means applying to all levels alike, and literally describes seats on opposite sides of a chessboard.

clue.text: Saturated turf by animal's lair

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a den is a wild animal's lair

explanation.surface: Soaked grass lies beside a creature's burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodden means thoroughly soaked, a synonym of saturated.

clue.text: Plant displayed in porch I designed

indicators.note: something displayed in a phrase is shown within it, so the answer lies inside these words

explanation.surface: A house plant is on show in a porch the speaker designed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from pORCH I Designed.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchid is a flowering plant with showy, often exotic blooms.

clue.text: Lard, once melted in kitchen utensil

indicators.note: melted fat loses its shape, so the letters lose their order

explanation.surface: Fat was once melted in a kitchen pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melted' rearranges LARD ONCE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a perforated bowl used in the kitchen to drain food.

clue.text: Runs excellent sprint

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for runs on a cricket scorecard
ace is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: An athlete runs a superb short dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprint is a short fast race over a short distance.

clue.text: Bend almost all of small shield

indicators.note: almost all of a word drops its final letter, so the last letter of the shield word goes

parts.note: a buckler is a small round shield

explanation.surface: A small shield is mostly bent out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To buckle is to bend or crumple under pressure.

clue.text: Left lout in lounge

parts.note: an oaf is a clumsy, boorish lout

explanation.surface: A yob is left behind in the lounge bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' looks like a room; it is a verb, to laze about. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf is to idle or lounge about doing nothing.

clue.text: Picked for team doing time

definitions.meaning: a player picked is in the side, the team
slang for being in prison serving a sentence

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means selected for the team; as one, it is slang for being in jail.

clue.text: Caught by a daring eccentric major-general at Balaclava

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bold, eccentric senior officer is captured during the Crimean battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges DARING into RDIGAN. Lord Cardigan, a major-general, led the Charge of the Light Brigade at Balaclava in 1854.
explanation.definitionFit: The 7th Earl of Cardigan commanded the Light Brigade at Balaclava, and the knitted jacket is named after him.
